project.title: Company-wide Provia rollout after the pilot

sources.title: Rollout request (chat, 2026-09-21)
sources.summary: The organization wants a company-wide rollout next week. The pilot has 2 completed cases and 8 blocked cases. No process owner is named. No pilot export, workflow YAML, org chart or SOP was supplied.

sections.title: Rollout request
sections.summary: Company-wide rollout wanted next week (week of 2026-09-28).

sections.title: Pilot results
sections.summary: 2 completed cases, 8 blocked cases. Cause of the blocks not supplied.

sections.title: Ownership
sections.summary: There is no named process owner.

groups.name: Process owner (pilot workflow)
groups.purpose: Placeholder for the person who owns the pilot process: answers the open decisions, accepts the workflow design, decides on blocked cases and signs off each rollout wave. The source says nobody holds this role today

flags.detail: The request states there is no named process owner. Decision D1 must name one before the rollout is treated as ready.
Ownership will sit with one person; a delegate for absences is part of decision D1.

groups.name: Pilot team
groups.purpose: The people who executed the pilot cases (2 completed, 8 blocked). They own the pilot workflow's actions until the workflow is registered in this manifest and its assignees are confirmed, and they act as reference users for the first expansion wave

flags.detail: The request does not name the pilot participants. Decision D5 asks for the list; no email was supplied, so none is proposed.

groups.name: Provia rollout support
groups.purpose: First-line support during the rollout: answers how-to questions, unblocks cases that are stuck for tooling reasons, keeps the blocked-case log and reports adoption measures to the process owner. Proposed by this plan, not named in the source

flags.detail: The source names nobody for support. Decision D5 asks who provides it; until then this group has no members.

decisions.question: Who is the process owner of the pilot workflow, and who is the delegate during absences? Without an owner nobody can accept the design, decide on the 8 blocked cases, own the access grants or sign off an expansion wave.
decisions.owner: Rollout sponsor (the manager requesting the company-wide rollout)

decisions.question: Supply the pilot workflow (YAML export or action list with assignees) and the case export of the 10 pilot cases, so the workflow can be registered in this manifest, ownership coverage checked and the 8 blocked cases triaged by cause.
decisions.owner: Process owner (D1); until named, the rollout sponsor

decisions.question: Accept the staged rollout (gate-based waves) instead of a company-wide switch next week? The pilot shows 2 completed and 8 blocked cases and no owner, which fails the expansion criteria of this plan. If the sponsor keeps the company-wide date, record that as an accepted risk with a named owner.
Confirm country, jurisdiction, language, timezone and currency. Angola / Africa/Luanda / AOA are a provisional starting context, not supplied by the source.

Name the pilot participants (group pilot_team), the support contacts (group rollout_support) and the departments and order of the expansion waves. Emails are needed before groups_apply_plan or manual group creation; none was supplied.

Who holds organization Owner/Admin in Provia and who administers group membership? These are organization roles, not workflow groups; the plan assumes they are not the same people as the workflow deciders.

Access matrix for the pilot workflow: who may open a case (organization-wide create_incident or a starter group), who holds edit on the design (proposed: process_owner) and whether any team needs view of every case. Cannot be written as data until the workflow is registered (D2).
